And while sitting through 12 Democratic primary debates seems nightmarish (think of all the corny, engineered viral moments we will be subjected to), a more rigorous primary process is preferable to a virtually nonexistent one like the Democrats pulled in 2024 . The DNC also wants to make sure these 12 debates attract the maximum number of eyeballs, and the organization says it "will seek to maximize the viewership of the debates, including by incorporating creators and influencers into the debate process." The announcement has already caught the attention of Hasan Piker, who wrote on X, "the debate will include creators and influencers you say?" According to The Washington Post , some influencers and content creators are already considering getting involved. articles.title: DNC limits 2028 primary candidates' ties to big-money groups
articles.author: Holly Otterbein
articles.summary: Democratic National Committee chair Ken Martin is moving to restrict candidates' ties to super PACs and dark-money groups in the party's 2028 presidential primary, a shift that could shake up the race for the White House. Why it matters: Most likely Democratic candidates for president were expected to rely on super PACs to boost their messaging — and go after other contenders. The DNC's new rules could complicate their plans and set up a clash between the party chair and soon-to-launch campaigns. Martin's plan will be a real-time test of whether party-driven campaign finance restrictions can function in a presidential primary that will follow a midterm election driven by billions in spending by PACs and dark-money groups. Zoom in: Under the rules that the DNC is announcing Monday, Democratic presidential candidates must disavow any super PACs or dark-money groups that either back them or attack their opponents in ads. If presidential hopefuls don't follow the guidelines, the DNC warns, they won't be allowed on the stage at primary debates. A DNC official said the change is backed by progressives such as Sens.
